Container.Name: RuneScape-Dragonwilds
Container.Overview:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds dedicated server. Native Linux binary via SteamCMD - no Proton or wine. First boot downloads about 1.5GB and settles at about 5GB.
Owner ID is required - your in-game Player ID, from the bottom of the in-game Settings menu. Without it the server runs but turns away every player, so this container refuses to start and says so in the log.
The fields below are written into DedicatedServer.ini on every start, so changing one and restarting takes effect. Anything else in that file is left alone.
Stopping does not save. The server autosaves every 5 minutes, so a stop costs at most that. For a clean stop, have players quit out through the game menu first.

Container.Changes:
###1.1.0 (2026-09-18) - IMPORTANT, and a correction to 1.0.3 below, which had this backwards. The game port must be the SAME NUMBER in three places: the Host Port, the Container Port behind the Edit button, and Server Port. This game advertises the port the server binds, so a port mapping cannot translate it. 1.0.3 told you to change only the host side; doing that gives a world that is listed, reports ready and heartbeats fine while every player who clicks it is sent to the container port instead. On the machine this was found on, that port belonged to an ARK container. - Server Port is a normal, required field again. 1.0.3 demoted it to the advanced section on the belief that it should never be changed; that belief was wrong. - The startup log now states the three-number rule every boot instead of warning about it. The old warning fired on correct setups and could not tell a correct one from a broken one, because nothing inside a container can read its own port mapping. - New Beacon Port field, UDP 8888. The server has always bound it; it was simply undocumented. It is a compiled constant and cannot be moved. Whether clients need to reach it is still untested. - The server also binds UDP 45453 for LAN discovery. There is deliberately no field for it: it is broadcast-based and cannot work across a Docker bridge at all. Use the in-game Worlds then Direct tab with host:port on a LAN, which needs game version 0.11.1 or newer.
###1.0.3 (2026-09-17) - Server Port is no longer a field you are meant to touch, and the whole class of silent breakage it caused is gone. Unraid keeps the Container Port fixed at 7777, so the server now always binds 7777 inside the container and the port mapping above points at it. Changing the port is one number again - Game Port - and it cannot disagree with anything. - What this fixes: Game Port and Server Port were the same two words in a different order, sitting next to each other, and changing the port the obvious way set both to the new number while the Container Port stayed 7777. Docker then forwarded to a port the server never bound. The server started, the log was clean, the container showed healthy and green, and no player could reach it, with no error anywhere. - Server Port moves to the advanced section and stays at 7777. It still matters under Network Type host, where there is no mapping and it is the only port number there is. - The startup warning added in 1.0.2 now names that distinction instead of describing the three-number rule that no longer applies.
###1.0.2 (2026-09-17) - The log now warns when Server Port is not 7777. Changing the port means changing three numbers - the Host Port, the Container Port and Server Port - and Unraid hides the Container Port behind the Edit button on the Game Port row. Miss it and the server starts, logs cleanly and shows green while no player can reach it, with no error anywhere. The warning is the signal that this is the thing to check. - Host networking is now documented as the supported way to run on a non-default port. Set Network Type to host and there is one number instead of three. - Correction to 1.0.0 below: 7777/udp is not the only socket the server binds. It also binds 8888/udp, a hardcoded world settings beacon, plus an ephemeral high port. 7777 remains the only port this container publishes and the only one to forward; whether anything needs to reach 8888 is untested.
###1.0.1 (2026-09-17) - Rewrote this description. It was three long paragraphs that opened by comparing this container to other servers; it is now shorter and stands on its own. No change to the image.
###1.0.0 (2026-09-14) Initial release.
- RuneScape: Dragonwilds dedicated server. The game ships a native Linux server binary, so this needs no Proton or wine - SteamCMD installs the Linux depot and the server runs directly. - Owner ID is required. It is your in-game Player ID, from the bottom of the in-game Settings menu. The container refuses to start without it, because the server itself does not: it would run, bind its port and refuse every player. - Server Name, World Name, Owner ID and both passwords are written into DedicatedServer.ini on every start, so changing one and restarting takes effect. Nothing else in that file is touched, including the ServerGuid. - Stopping the container does not save - the game's only save-on-exit path is its in-game quit flow, unreachable from outside, and it has no RCON or console. The server autosaves every 5 minutes instead, so a stop costs at most 5 minutes. Have players quit out in-game for a clean stop. Raise Unraid's container stop timeout to at least 45 seconds. - Player cap is 6. It is not a setting in this game's config file, so there is no field for it. - UDP 7777 is the only port the server binds. If something else on this box already uses it, change it here.
Container.Requires: About 5GB once installed, from a 1.5GB download, so allow 8GB of free space for saves and updates. Roughly 2GB of RAM plus 1GB per player, so 8GB for a full server - the cap is 6 players. The array is fine; a cache drive or SSD makes world loads and saves noticeably quicker.

Config.Name: Game Port
Config.Description: Game traffic, UDP, and the port to forward on your router. To move it you must set THREE things to the same number: this Host Port box, the Container Port behind the Edit button on this row, and Server Port below. That is not a Docker convention - this game advertises the port the server BINDS, so a port mapping cannot translate it. Publish 7780 against a server bound to 7777 and your world is listed, reports ready, heartbeats fine, logs no errors, and every player who clicks it is sent to 7777 instead. If something else on this box already listens on the number you pick, Docker refuses to start this container - pick another.

Config.Name: Server Port
Config.Description: The port the server binds, and the port it advertises to other players - those are the same number and nothing can separate them. It must equal Game Port above, BOTH the Host Port and the Container Port. Under Network Type host there is no mapping and this is the only port number there is.

Config.Name: Beacon Port
Config.Description: The world settings beacon. The server binds this on top of the game port and the number is compiled into the game, so it cannot be moved - which also means only one of these containers per box can publish it. Whether clients actually need to reach it is UNTESTED; nothing has been reported broken without it. Publishing it costs nothing if 8888 is free. The server binds a third socket too, UDP 45453 for LAN discovery, which is deliberately not here: it is broadcast-based and Docker bridge networks do not carry the host LAN broadcasts it needs, so publishing it would promise something that cannot work. See the README.

Config.Name: Game Files
Config.Description: Where the server, saves and config live. About 5GB - see Requires below. Your worlds are under RSDragonwilds/Saved/SaveGames and your config is RSDragonwilds/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/DedicatedServer.ini.

Config.Name: SteamCMD
Config.Description: SteamCMD itself. Small, and shareable with other SteamCMD containers.

Config.Name: Owner ID
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Your in-game Player ID: open RuneScape: Dragonwilds, go to Settings, and it is at the bottom of that menu with a copy button next to it. The server will not serve anyone without this, and this container refuses to start without it rather than run something that looks healthy and turns every player away.

Config.Name: Server Name
Config.Description: Name shown in the server browser. Applied on every restart.

Config.Name: World Name
Config.Description: Names the world the server creates on first boot, and the save file it uses - SaveGames/<name>.sav. This is most likely also the name players type to find you under Worlds then Public, and it is case-sensitive, so pick something you are happy telling people. Changing it after first boot starts a NEW world; the old one stays on disk and setting this name back returns to it. It does not rename anything.

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: Anyone who enters this in the game's Pause Menu, Settings, Server Management tab becomes an admin on this server. Leave it blank and the server generates a random one on first boot and prints it in the log - so setting one here is the easier path. Changing it revokes admin from everyone who used the old one.

Config.Name: World Password
Config.Description: Join password. Leave blank for a server anyone can join. This supersedes any password stored in the world itself.

Config.Name: Extra Game Parameters
Config.Description: Appended to the launch line verbatim. Nothing routine needs this - every documented setting lives in DedicatedServer.ini, not on the command line. The one known use is attempting to raise the 6-player cap, which is not in that file: -ini:Game:[/Script/Engine.GameSession]:MaxPlayers=8 - though whether a value above 6 does anything is unverified.

Config.Name: Validate Files
Config.Description: Set to true to have SteamCMD verify every file on the next start. Slow on a 5GB install. Use it after a crash or a failed update.

Config.Name: Stop Timeout
Config.Description: Seconds to wait for the engine to shut down before force killing. This is not a save window - shutdown does not save, and the 5-minute autosave is what protects the world. Measured teardown is about 2 seconds. Also raise Unraid's own container stop timeout to at least 45.

Config.Name: Steam Username
Config.Description: Leave blank. The Dragonwilds server downloads anonymously.

Config.Name: UID
Config.Description: User ID. 99 is the Unraid default. It must not be 0 - the server refuses to run as root and aborts on startup.

Config.Name: GID
Config.Description: Group ID. 100 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: Data Permissions
Config.Description: Mode applied to the top of the server directory.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: umask for files the server creates. 000 keeps them editable over the share.
